subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Infinite Scroll and Engagement Loops
description: A fast breakdown of Infinite Scroll and Engagement Loops for builders.

hook.text: You open the app for 2 minutes. An hour passes. The feed has no bottom. That is not a bug. It is the business model.

buildup.text: Infinite scroll removes natural stopping points. Without a page break, there's no pause for the brain to decide.

discovery.text: Variable reward schedules drive engagement. Unpredictable content, like a slot machine, keeps you scrolling.

twist.text: Aza Raskin, who invented infinite scroll, now regrets it. He estimates it wastes 200,000 human lifetimes per day.

climax.text: Set a timer before opening addictive apps. Without an external stop signal, the app will never tell you to leave.

punchline.text: The app has no stop button. You must build your own.

quiz.question: Why is infinite scroll so engaging?
options: It loads content faster than paginated feeds
It removes stopping points so the brain never decides to leave
Users prefer scrolling over clicking buttons

details.summary: Infinite scroll eliminates natural stopping points, keeping users scrolling through content or products indefinitely. This design exploits the seeking behavior of the dopamine system, creating compulsive engagement without conscious decision to continue.
details.whyItMatters: Infinite scroll and engagement loops are the primary mechanisms behind addictive app and website design. They maximize time on site and ad exposure by removing friction points where users would naturally disengage.
takeaways: Removing stopping points prevents natural disengagement decisions
Variable content rewards keep the dopamine-seeking system active
Infinite scroll increases page views but can reduce purchase quality

faq.question: How does infinite scroll affect purchasing behavior?
faq.answer: It increases browsing time and exposure to products but can reduce purchase satisfaction. Without natural stopping points, consumers view more items but become overwhelmed, leading to either impulsive choices or abandonment.

faq.question: Why is infinite scroll considered a dark pattern?
faq.answer: Because it removes the user's ability to make a conscious stopping decision. Traditional pagination creates natural breakpoints where users evaluate whether to continue. Infinite scroll bypasses this self-regulation mechanism.
